question: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Railways'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Dalhousie is often referred to as the 'Father of Indian Railways' because he was instrumental in introducing railways in India.
 
• During his tenure as the Governor-General of India, the first railway line from Mumbai to Thane was inaugurated in 1853.
 
• Lord Dalhousie believed that the railways would help in the economic development of India by facilitating the movement of goods and people.
 
• He laid down a comprehensive plan for the construction of railway lines across India, which became the foundation for the railway network that exists today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Ripon**

 
 
• Lord Ripon served as the Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884.
 
• He is known for his liberal policies and for repealing the Vernacular Press Act.
 
• He introduced local self-government in India, which was a significant step towards decentralization.
 
• He is also remembered for the Ilbert Bill controversy, which sought to allow Indian judges to try British offenders.
 
 
 
• **Lord Irwin**
 
 
• Lord Irwin served as the Viceroy of India from 1926 to 1931.
 
• He is known for the Irwin Declaration of 1929, which promised dominion status for India.
 
• During his tenure, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in 1931, which marked a truce between Mahatma Gandhi and the British government.
 
• He also faced the Civil Disobedience Movement led by the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Lord Minto**
 
 
• Lord Minto served as the Viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910.
 
• He is known for the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909, which introduced separate electorates for Muslims in India.
 
• These reforms were a significant step towards constitutional reforms in British India.
 
• He also dealt with the rise of revolutionary activities during his tenure.
